intro: What to say in an emergency and at the lost-property office.

el empleado.nota: The feminine form is la empleada.

la oficina de objetos perdidos.pron: la o-fi-SI-na de ob-HEK-tos per-DI-dos (seseo) / o-fi-THI-na de ob-HEK-tos per-DI-dos (distinción)

he olvidado.en: I have forgotten; I have left behind

la cartera.en: the wallet (Spain; often a handbag in Latin America)
la cartera.nota: La billetera is also used for wallet in many places.

la billetera.en: the wallet (common in many Latin American varieties)

el móvil.en: the mobile phone (celular in many Latin American countries)

bloques.texto:
To shout: **¡Socorro!** **¡Ayuda!** **¡Cuidado!** **¡Fuego!**

To ask for help formally: **Llame a** una ambulancia or **a** los bomberos. In Spain and across the EU, **112** reaches emergency services free of charge.

In much of Spain, recent completed events often use the **pretérito perfecto**: **Ha habido** un accidente. **He olvidado** el bolso. **He perdido** el pasaporte. In many Latin American varieties, the **pretérito indefinido** is common for completed events: **hubo**, **olvidé**, **perdí**. Usage varies by region.

In **he olvidado**, **haber** + participle shows a recent action that still matters now: the bag is still missing.

At the lost-property office: **Quiero rellenar un formulario** (fill in a form). You may hear **¿Qué ha pasado? / ¿Qué pasó?** and **¿Dónde ha sido? / ¿Dónde fue?**. To describe an object in the past, use the **imperfecto**: **era** negro y **llevaba** un llavero azul.

frases.es: Buenos días. Quiero rellenar un formulario. He perdido el bolso.
frases.en: Good morning. I want to fill in a form. I have lost my bag.

frases.es: En el metro, hace una hora.
frases.en: On the underground, an hour ago.
What did you have in the bag?

frases.es: La cartera, el móvil y el pasaporte.
frases.en: My wallet, my phone and my passport.
analisis: La cartera, el móvil y el pasaporte

frases.en: Thank you. What was the bag like?

frases.es: Era negro y llevaba un llavero azul.
frases.en: It was black and had a blue keyring on it.

opciones.texto: I have left my wallet behind.
opciones.explicacion: He olvidado means I have forgotten or left behind; la cartera is the wallet.
He olvidado: I have left it behind.
That would be he comprado la cartera.

bloques.pregunta: Complete, with usted: call an ambulance, please.

opciones.Llamar: A request needs the command form.

bloques.pregunta: Where do you ask about a lost bag?
bloques.correcta: en la oficina de objetos perdidos

bloques.pregunta: Complete: I have lost my passport.
Complete the description: the bag was black.

opciones.era: Era is the natural choice for describing the bag in the past.
opciones.fue: Fue presents the state as a bounded event, which is not the natural description here.
opciones.estuvo: Estuvo presents a temporary, bounded state; era is the natural description here.

bloques.traduccion: I want to fill in a form.

bloques.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (60–80 words).** Write what you would say on the phone to the emergency services after an accident: what happened, where, how many people.

**Speak (about 1 minute).** Practise aloud calling 112: say who you are, where you are and what has happened, clearly and slowly.
